title: Streaming protocol linter and schema smoke suite for API compatibility
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: build a lightweight, deterministic linter and a compact smoke-test suite that validates frame-level streaming semantics, structured-output NDJSON/JSON-stream schema fidelity, and tool/function-call handshake behavior across model shims and SDKs. This ticket covers: (1) a protocol-level linter that detects violations (out-of-order frames, missing end markers, improper chunk boundaries), (2) a schema validator for streamed NDJSON and partial-JSON chunks used by structured outputs and tool responses, and (3) a compact OSS smoke harness that runs these checks across the three canonical model shims + SDK streaming implementations in CI.

Why: We have recurring regressions where subtle changes in tokenizer/stream buffering or in the model shim produce interleavings that break downstream tool parsers or the Console's structured-output analytics. Current tests catch higher-level regressions but not frame-level or partial-JSON edgecases. A protocol linter plus a small representative prompt corpus will make these compatibility regressions easier to triage and block changes before they reach customers.

Scope and deliverables: 
- A reusable linter library (python + node bindings) that consumes streaming frames (simulated network frames and SDK frames) and emits deterministic diagnostics and a severity score. The linter includes rule modules: frame-order, end-marker presence, continuation semantics, JSON-chunk reassembly, and toolcall handshake verification.
- A compact smoke test harness (OSS-friendly) that executes ~120 focused scenarios derived from our customer-facing issues: partial-json-splits, interleaved-toolcalls, trailing-comma-resilience, mid-token splits, and KV-cache-priming sequences.
- Integration with CI: failing linter rules marked as blocking for P0/P1 API changes; an opt-out flag for experimental branches; nightly matrix runs against three model-shim builds.
- Documentation and onboarding guide for engineers and SDK teams describing how to run the linter locally and how to author new rules and scenarios.

Out-of-scope: exhaustive golden-prompt corpus; full behavioral fingerprinting across end-to-end apps (this is a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Linter library published in monorepo and importable by runtime and SDKs
Smoke harness with 120 scenarios added under tests/stream-lint and runnable in CI
CI gating: PRs touching streaming code fail the gate when >1 P1 violation is introduced
Documentation and quickstart added to Confluence and README in repo
Nightly matrix completes against three model-shim images with pass/fail dashboard
test_matrix_and_steps: Seed corpus: 120 scenarios covering partial-json, interleaved-toolcalls, mid-token-splits, dangling-end, and kv-cache-priming
Run linter against synthetic frame traces generated by model-shim + SDK emulators
Record diagnostics and severity; failures with severity >= high surface as CI failures
Integrate linter into unit and e2e CI stages; nightly full matrix for model-shim variants
When a lint rule fires, attach a minimal repro trace and link to suggested remediation in the comment
